name: Agent 37

modes.label: Standard (no dedicated cores)
modes.note: Shared CPU (the pricing page contrasts it with Performance, which "run[s] on dedicated cores"); no fair-share baseline published. Rates = $0.80/vCPU-mo, $0.70/GB-mo ÷ 730, metered per minute (billing docs). Four shapes, 4 vCPU ceiling on every type (instance-sizing docs, 2026-11-08): 2/4, 4/8, 4/16, 4/32; size hour = compute only, disk billed separately at $0.09/GB-mo.

modes.label: Dedicated Performance
modes.note: "Performance instances run on dedicated cores, at 4x the compute rate" (pricing page): $3.20/vCPU-mo, $2.80/GB-mo ÷ 730, per-minute metering. Same four shapes (4 vCPU ceiling); disk 2-100 GB on every shape (instance-sizing docs).

modes.label: VM instance (full VM, own kernel + KVM)
modes.note: "type": "vm" on create: "a full Linux virtual machine with its own kernel and KVM hardware virtualization"; Docker, Compose, buildx, k3s, /dev/kvm inside. "compute meters at 2.5x the default rate: a VM's RAM is reserved for it alone and its vCPUs are its own" ($2.00/vCPU-mo, $1.75/GB-mo ÷ 730); disk unchanged at $0.09/GB-mo. Same four shapes as the default type (2/4, 4/8, 4/16, 4/32; 4 vCPU ceiling), disk 2-100 GB on every shape (instance-sizing docs). Allowed before the first top-up ("of any template, size, or type, VMs included"); create needs one day of the running rate in the wallet. No init system (systemd entrypoint unsupported); cold-boots on start and on every resize. Type is fixed for the instance's life.

modes.label: Managed OpenClaw/Hermes hosting (flat monthly per instance)
modes.note: Flat subscription per agent instance, now listed on agent37.com/personal (no longer on /pricing, which is Cloud API only): Basic $3.99, Plus $9.99, Pro $29.99, Max $99.99 per month (hour = monthly price / 730; requires_always_on because the fee is due whether or not it runs). Includes AI credits ($1/-/$5/$20 per month; Plus and above bundle free models). Free tier: 1 vCPU/4 GB/2 GB, sleeps after 15 minutes idle, $0.20 of the default model. Browser-managed product distinct from the Cloud API, hence alt.

plans.name: Free (no top-up)
plans.note: Up to 3 awake instances "of any template, size, or type, VMs included"; one-time $5 starter credit once a card is added. Sleeping and stopped instances do not count.

plans.name: Wallet (any top-up)
plans.note: 10 awake instances after the first top-up. Sleeping and stopped instances never count.

plans.name: Wallet ($50 lifetime top-ups)
plans.note: 50 awake instances once cumulative top-ups reach $50 (prepaid credit, spent on usage)

plans.name: Wallet ($250 lifetime top-ups)
plans.note: 200 awake instances once cumulative top-ups reach $250

plans.name: Wallet ($1,000 lifetime top-ups)
plans.note: 1,000 awake instances once cumulative top-ups reach $1,000 (prepaid credit, spent on usage). Above 1,000: email vishnu@agent37.com or dashboard chat.

caveats: Cloud API uses monthly resource rates divided by 730 then by 60 for minute metering. Running and start/stop transitions bill allocation, NOT measured CPU utilization.

Dedicated Performance compute is 4x CPU and RAM, VM instances 2.5x, disk unchanged on both. Managed hosting (agent37.com/personal) is a separate flat monthly per-instance product; model allowances are not compute credits.

Instance cap (awake instances at once): 3 before the first top-up, 10 after any top-up, 50 at $50 lifetime top-ups, 200 at $250, 1,000 at $1,000; not a monthly fee. "Sleeping and stopped ones never count, so you can keep as many as you like" (billing docs, checked 2026-11-08). Create needs one day of balance, not a debit.

Cold parked compressed files $0.03/GB-month versus reserved hot disk $0.09. Non-payment suspension is unbilled and deletes after 30 days; ordinary persistence is until deletion. Default auto-topup buys $25 below $10.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.

Snapshot/state rate set to the cold-storage rate ($0.03/GB-mo on compressed bytes) that long-idle sleepers are moved to; a stopped-but-hot instance keeps paying $0.09 per reserved disk GB (billed as disk). No named-snapshot product documented; to copy state into a new instance, fork it (disk copy, the fork boots fresh).
Rates verified against the public billing docs 2026-09-28 ($0.80/vCPU-mo, $0.70/GB-mo, per-minute metering), not on a live account; they are far below peers, treat as unverified in practice.

Agent 37 sells two CPU tiers: Standard does not reserve cores for you (no guaranteed share published); Performance "run[s] on dedicated cores" at 4x the vCPU price. Only Standard carries the caveat, and only under sustained CPU load.

No published create-rate or API rate limits (only 1 on-demand backup per instance per 15 min). Wake from checkpoint 'a few seconds' (5-15 s via start); cold-storage/relocation wake ~2 min (billed at disk rate). SSH documented (root by default).

Isolation: "Every sandbox is enforced by gVisor" (agent37.com/cloud) for default and Performance instances. A separate "type": "vm" instance is a full VM with its own kernel and KVM (modelled as the vm mode, 2.5x default compute): Docker, Compose, k3s, Docker-in-Docker and /dev/kvm work there, not on the default type.
Creating an instance requires one day of its running rate in the wallet (not debited); 503 no_capacity / 409 capacity_unavailable possible when hosts are full.

Nested virtualization / Docker inside: no on the default gVisor type (no /dev/kvm, "cannot run a Docker daemon"); yes on the vm type (/dev/kvm present, dockerd preinstalled in agent37-ubuntu). Workloads that need Docker or KVM price on the vm mode.

Shapes (instance-sizing docs, 2026-11-08): 2 vCPU/4 GB, 4/8, 4/16, 4/32; "4 vCPU is the ceiling on every instance type". Disk on the default type: 2-12 GB (2/4), 2-20 GB (4/8), 2-40 GB (4/16), 2-80 GB (4/32). "A VM or performance instance takes 2-100 GB of disk on every shape." The engine has no per-shape disk cap field, so a large disk on the default type is not forced onto a bigger shape.

Burstable: experimental instance type for low average CPU and RAM usage, from $1/month (instance-sizing docs); needs workspace enablement and has no published rates or shapes, so it is not modelled as a mode.
Starter credit is $5 (billing docs, /pricing and /cloud agree as of 2026-10-14), once per account and card, before the first top-up.

Compliance: SOC 2 Type I, Type II in progress (agent37.com/cloud). Regions: us, eu (France) and ap-south (India, Mumbai), same price; eu and ap-south run VM and Performance instances only, and backups and control-plane records stay in the US (docs, checked 2026-11-08). The docs glossary still says "Runs on dedicated servers in the United States".

Desktop: the stock agent37-hermes template has a headless browser only. A desktop needs one build of the official hermes-vnc-desktop example (desktop = diy), or the agent37-ubuntu VM type, which ships XFCE with Firefox on port 6080. No screenshot/click computer-use API: "it does not bundle a general desktop-control SDK" (desktop docs, 2026-11-08).

fleet.verification: Cloud API requires a card on file for starter credit; prepaid Stripe top-ups ($5 minimum) unlock higher tiers. Additional ID/KYC requirements not specified.
fleet.tiers: Awake instances at once: before first top-up 3 (any size or type, VMs included); any top-up: 10; $50 lifetime top-ups: 50; $250: 200; $1,000: 1,000. Above 1,000 contact vishnu@agent37.com or dashboard chat.
fleet.notes: Official billing docs describe automatic cumulative-top-up limits per workspace. The cap counts only awake instances; sleeping and stopped ones never count. 10/50/200/1,000 fleets have published funding paths; above 1,000 needs a reviewed increase with no published turnaround. Starter credit is $5.
fleet.max_disk_gib: Default type: 2-12 GB (2/4), 2-20 GB (4/8), 2-40 GB (4/16), 2-80 GB (4/32); VM and Performance: 2-100 GB on every shape; images max 8 GB; Dockerfile build 45 min max, context 1 GB

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: In-memory state usually survives a wake, but it is not guaranteed: treat anything that must outlive a sleep as a file.
snapshot_auto.note: Opt-in auto_sleep: after idle_timeout_seconds (default 900 s, 5 min to 1 day) with no bytes through the instance URLs 'the platform checkpoints it' to sleeping; any request to a URL, start, exec or update restores it in a few seconds. Memory/processes included when the checkpoint restores; if the wake has to rebuild (moved host / cold storage / restore failure) it boots fresh with disk kept. Explicit stop discards the checkpoint. Also nightly disk backups in 7 rotating slots (not a snapshot_auto).

snapshot_on_demand.quote: You can also take a backup on demand, into a separate slot that only your next on-demand backup replaces.
snapshot_on_demand.note: POST /v1/instances/{id}/backups: live, crash-consistent, disk data only (/home/node and /home/linuxbrew), no memory; one manual slot, max 1 per 15 min; restore is in place only (POST /restore recreates the container, in-memory state lost). Nightly backups fill 7 rotating slots. To copy state into a new instance, use fork (POST /v1/instances/{id}/fork, disk copy).

harness_api.quote: The core call: POST /v1/responses on your instance URL runs a turn through your agent, streams or returns the result, and continues the thread.
harness_api.note: Harnesses: hermes, openclaw, claude-code, codex, grok, opencode, pi (selected per turn with an 'agent' field). SSE streaming with reconnect, session list/read/rename/delete (GET /v1/sessions), per-turn model/reasoning_effort, crons that fire agent turns, health probe per harness.

ingress_rules.quote: An instance needs no public IP address. Every port it listens on has its own HTTPS URL, and the platform edge checks your key.
ingress_rules.note: Every port URL requires the X-Agent37-Key header or a time-boxed signed URL (401 otherwise); public (unauthenticated) ports are opt-in per port via the Hosting API and platform ports (gateway, terminal, SSH 22022) cannot be made public; SSH only via authenticated WebSocket tunnel. API keys can carry an IP allowlist (up to 20 IPs/CIDRs), but signed URLs and public ports bypass it.

secret_proxy.quote: Every instance ships with managed LLM, Brave search, and Composio credentials: metered at cost, gated by a per-instance budget you control.
secret_proxy.note: Instances get a per-instance AGENT37_MANAGED_TOKEN plus AGENT37_LLM_PROXY_URL (OpenAI-compatible, https://api.agent37.com/llm/v1), a Composio MCP proxy (Gmail/Slack/Notion etc. OAuth held by the platform) and a paid-tools MCP; real provider keys never enter the sandbox, but the per-instance platform token does. No generic register-any-credential HTTP proxy; your own keys (OpenAI/xAI/Anthropic) go in as env vars or config files on the instance. The BYO-model kit's LLM proxy is customer-hosted, not first-party. Non-HTTP protocols not covered.

docker_inside.quote: The default gVisor instance type cannot run a Docker daemon.
docker_inside.note: Card-level value is for the default (and Performance) gVisor instances. The "vm" mode overrides it to true: "Docker, Compose, and buildx. Build and run containers, including Docker-in-Docker workloads and containers that need privileged mode or their own networks."

anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Agent37 is persistent agent-sandbox hosting (Hermes/OpenClaw/Claude Code/etc. on always-on Linux instances with a Chromium browser stack); no stealth/fingerprint-evasion feature against bot detection is documented anywhere in the docs or pricing pages.

captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No CAPTCHA-solving feature or add-on is documented anywhere in the Agent37 docs, pricing, or managed-services pages.

fork.quote: Copy an instance into an independent instance with its own id, URLs, budget, and billing.
fork.note: Disk-only copy (processes do not carry over; the fork boots fresh). Source may be running, stopped or sleeping (not in cold storage). cpu and memory may move in either direction on the fork; disk can only match or grow. Works on VM instances too.

fork_running.quote: The source must be `running`, `stopped`, or `sleeping`; one parked in cold storage has to be started first.
fork_running.note: A running source can be forked; memory is not copied (memory_snapshot_fork stays false).

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: What is copied is the source's disk, not its memory
memory_snapshot_fork.note: Fork exists but copies disk only.

volume_attach.quote: `/home/node` and `/home/linuxbrew` are persistent volumes bind-mounted over your image at runtime. The volume is created empty...
volume_attach.note: Each instance has exactly one built-in persistent volume (its own disk under /home); there is no documented API to attach additional/extra persistent volumes to a machine.

volume_shared.quote: **Separate customers.** Sessions on one instance share its disk. When customers must not see each other's files, give each one its own self-hosted environment and instance.
volume_shared.note: Storage is scoped per-instance; there is no documented feature to mount one volume across several running instances simultaneously.

own_agent_api.quote: Which agent harness runs the turn, `hermes`, `openclaw`, `claude-code`, `codex`, `grok`, `opencode`, or `pi`.
own_agent_api.note: Agent37's own harnesses (Hermes, OpenClaw) are driven through the exact same generic /v1/responses harness API used for third-party coding harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi); there is no separate first-party API dedicated to a distinct own browser/computer-use/research task agent beyond that shared harness API.

mcp_server.quote: A Composio MCP server, scoped to this instance's own entity ... A pay-per-call MCP server at $AGENT37_PERFLO_MCP_URL
mcp_server.note: The MCP servers Agent37 ships (Composio, Perflo) are tools an agent running inside an instance calls out to; they are not an MCP server exposed to control/manage Agent37 sandboxes themselves (create/start/stop instances) from an external MCP client.

lang_python.quote: [hermes-base] ships Hermes with its browser stack (Chromium, Playwright), the gateway that serves the chat API, and a general toolchain: git, Python 3 with uv, Node.js, build tools.

lang_node.quote: a general toolchain: git, Python 3 with uv, Node.js, build tools.
lang_node.note: Base images are also built FROM node:22-bookworm-slim.

egress_allowlist.quote: The worker only makes outbound HTTPS calls to `api.anthropic.com`. The instance needs no public URL, open port, or webhook.
egress_allowlist.note: No provider-side outbound allow/deny-list, no-internet mode, or security-group egress rule feature is documented; instances appear to have ordinary unrestricted outbound internet access.

egress_http_rules.quote: An instance needs no public IP address. Every port it listens on has its own HTTPS URL, and the platform edge checks your key.
egress_http_rules.note: Documented access controls (ingress_rules, signed URLs, IP allowlists on API keys) all govern inbound access to the instance's own ports, not outbound HTTP method/path-level egress filtering; no such egress rule feature is documented.

guest_firewall.quote: Every sandbox is enforced by gVisor
guest_firewall.note: derived: isolation is gVisor (a container with a user-space kernel/netstack), not a full VM/microVM, so the guest_firewall heuristic (full VM + root=true ⇒ nftables/iptables work) does not apply; gVisor's own netstack does not support the kernel netfilter machinery iptables/nftables rely on.

static_egress_ip.note: No fixed/dedicated outbound IP product is documented anywhere in the pricing or docs pages; instances have no public IPv4 at all (ipv4_available: false).

gpu.quote: Performance instances run on dedicated cores, at 4x the compute rate
gpu.note: Only two CPU/RAM tiers (Standard shared, Performance dedicated-core) are sold; no GPU instance type, GPU pricing, or GPU option appears anywhere on the pricing page or docs.

windows.quote: Build for `linux/amd64` even on an Apple Silicon Mac ... An arm64 image is rejected during registration.
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Every instance runs a linux/amd64 image; there is no Windows machine type.

macos.quote: Build for `linux/amd64` even on an Apple Silicon Mac (`docker build --platform linux/amd64 ...`).
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Instances are Linux containers only; macOS is only mentioned as a possible local developer machine for building images, not an instance OS.

self_host.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Agent37 is a hosted multi-tenant platform (own infrastructure, workspaces, wallet billing); no on-prem/self-hosted deployment of the Agent37 control plane is documented.

byoc.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No option to deploy the managed service into a customer's own cloud account is documented anywhere in the pricing or docs pages.

open_source.note: The core Agent37 platform (hosting API, gateway, billing) is closed/proprietary; only some hosted third-party harnesses (Pi, OpenCode, n8n) are themselves open source, which is not the same as the product being open source.

hipaa.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No HIPAA-eligibility or BAA mention was found anywhere in the pricing page, docs, or llms-full.txt after a full-text search.

sso.quote: Both planes take the same `sk_live_` key ... Mint keys in the dashboard.
sso.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Authentication is by workspace API key (sk_live_) plus email sign-in on the dashboard; no SAML/OIDC single sign-on feature is documented.

eu_data_residency.quote: Backups and the instance's own control-plane record (its id, shape, and status) are stored in the US; if that matters for your use case, email [vishnu@agent37.com](mailto:vishnu@agent37.com) before you build on it.
eu_data_residency.note: An eu (France) region exists for VM and Performance instances, and the instance, its disk and what it writes stay there; backups and control-plane records stay in the US, so full EU data residency is not offered.

max_session_h.quote: There is no time limit on a turn; the stream stays open until the agent is done.
max_session_h.note: Instances are always-on until explicitly stopped or auto-slept purely on idle bytes-through-URL (idle_timeout_seconds, 5 min to 1 day); there is no documented maximum wall-clock session/instance lifetime, so this is 'none' like a VM that runs until you stop it.

nested_virt.quote: Android emulators. /dev/kvm is present inside the machine, so an AVD boots with hardware acceleration instead of crawling.
nested_virt.note: false holds only for the default gVisor type (no /dev/kvm). The "vm" mode overrides to true per the quote above.

public_ipv4.quote: An instance needs no public IP address. Every port it listens on has its own HTTPS URL, and the platform edge checks your key.
public_ipv4.note: Also stated directly for SSH: 'The instance has no public IP and no listening port on the internet.' Confirms no public IPv4 per machine; access is via per-port HTTPS URLs/signed URLs/custom domains only.

arm64.quote: Build for linux/amd64 even on an Apple Silicon Mac (docker build --platform linux/amd64 ...). An arm64 image is rejected during registration.
arm64.note: Explicit: custom images must be amd64; arm64 images are rejected outright. No arm64 instance shape offered anywhere in docs/pricing.

live_resize.quote: POST /v1/instances/{id}/resize grows a running instance to a bigger size. The body uses the same vocabulary as create's resources, and omitted fields keep their current value, so { "disk": 10 } grows disk alone and { "cpu": 4, "memory": 8 } moves up a shape (disk carries over unchanged). Resize only grows: any request that would shrink a dimension returns 400, and moving to a smaller size means creating a new instance.
live_resize.note: Corrected from false to true: the API explicitly resizes CPU/RAM (and disk) of a running instance without recreating it (400 on the create-a-new-instance path is only for shrinking). Caveat: grow-only, no shrink; shrinking requires creating a new instance. VM instances: resize cold-boots the machine (in-memory state lost), so the vm mode sets live_resize false.

egress_ip_type.quote: The worker only makes outbound HTTPS calls to `api.anthropic.com`. The instance needs no public URL, open port, or webhook.
egress_ip_type.note: derived: instances have no public IPv4 and no static/dedicated egress IP product is documented (static_egress_ip: false); outbound traffic runs through Agent37's own cloud hosts. No residential or mobile proxy/egress feature is mentioned anywhere in the docs or pricing pages, so outbound IPs are ordinary shared datacenter addresses on the provider's hosting infrastructure, not a distinguished static-datacenter, residential, or mobile IP product.

usage_api.quote: GET /v1/usage?from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD returns everything the workspace spent, by UTC day, by instance, and by model. GET /v1/instances/{id}/usage returns a monthly rollup. Response includes total_micros, by_integration (compute, llm, brave, composio, perflo each with cost_micros), by_model, da
usage_api.note: granularity: per-instance; cost: yes; Workspace-level usage API returns per-instance breakdown; instance-level API available for single-instance monthly rollup. Costs reported in USD micros. Compute metered per minute, managed usage metered per call.

soc2.quote: SOC 2 Type I and readiness reports on request.
soc2.note: SOC 2 Type I; the same page badges Type II as in progress.

regions.quote: Where the instance runs: `us`, `eu` (France), or `ap-south` (India, Mumbai). The price is the same in all three.
regions.note: Set at create, fixed for the instance's life. "`us` is the only region that runs every instance type. `eu` and `ap-south` run VM and Performance instances"; a default create there returns 503 no_capacity. Mode regions follow this: standard us only; performance and vm us/eu/asia.

desktop.quote: Build the desktop recipe and the same browser runs on a screen you can open in a tab, watch live, and take control of when a site needs a human. Other templates include different tools; a browser is not installed on every instance.
desktop.how: build the official hermes-vnc-desktop example into a template (one cloud build with npx agent37 templates build), then open port 6901 /vnc.html; or create agent37-ubuntu with type vm, which ships an XFCE desktop on port 6080
desktop.note: Default gVisor type: no desktop on the stock template, one documented build adds it. The vm mode sets desktop true: "plus an XFCE desktop with Firefox in the browser" (vm-instances docs).

computer_use.quote: Agent37 provides the machine, desktop, exec, and SSH; it does not bundle a general desktop-control SDK or session recording service.
computer_use.note: No screenshot + click API. The page says your own harness can install its own screenshot, click and typing tools on the Ubuntu VM; that is a generic install, not a documented provider path, so not diy. The stock Hermes agent drives a headless browser (browser stays true).

locations_quote: Where the instance runs: `us`, `eu` (France), or `ap-south` (India, Mumbai). The price is the same in all three.
locations_note: eu and ap-south run VM and Performance instances only; the default type runs in us only.
perf_source: ComputeSDK (each provider at its SDK default size and runtime): burst 2.35 s median at 100 at once, 100% succeeded (2026-11-06); DAX clone + install + typecheck 110.02 s (2026-11-06, one run; sandbox saw 4 CPUs / 16 GiB x86). https://github.com/computesdk/benchmarks/tree/main/results
